analysis:
Examined the changes in the Prompting directory and ProviderLoop+ErrorMapping.swift. They fall into four groups.

1. Stop-string scoping. ChatTemplateFixes.stopStringScope (line 136), GPTOSSHarmonyTemplateFix.finalChannelStopScope (line 45), ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope (line 30) and the new ReasoningStopScope.swift limit client stop strings to the Harmony final channel. For Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1 and Gemma4 they exclude reasoning and tool-call spans. This is a correctness and availability behavior change, not a trust-boundary change. Stop strings are client-supplied. Their scope affects only when generation ends, so it cannot expose plaintext or bypass the encryption, attestation or authorization controls (A-001, TB-002, TB-007). A possible resource-exhaustion concern is that a stop string might never match inside excluded spans, so generation runs to max_tokens. That is bounded by the existing token limits and the cancellation controls (T-010), and the CBv2StopStringScope implementation was not supplied, so it is unverified.

2. .logprobs enum case handling. GLM5NextResponseFormat.swift line 101 and JSONAnswerFormat.swift line 81 add `.logprobs` to the exhaustive switches. In GLM5NextResponseFormatOutput.withholding, `.logprobs` events are returned immediately, unlike content, which is withheld until validation. Logprobs could therefore stream tokens of the answer text before the JSON validation completes. Whether the `.logprobs` event carries token text depends on the unseen MLXLMServer definition, and it reaches the consumer, who owns the prompt, so it is not a cross-tenant leak. It is a minor integrity or contract concern: unvalidated content could be exposed ahead of the typed 422. I did not raise it as a finding because it cannot be confirmed from the supplied source. A deeper pass should check whether logprobs carry token strings and whether the GLM engine ever emits them.

3. Error mapping. ProviderLoop+ErrorMapping.swift line 249 maps the new .responseFormatCutOffByMaxTokens case to 422. This is benign. Only the patch excerpt was supplied, with no base or head text.

4. The prefix-cache threat T-041 is unaffected. No cacheSalt, KV or SSD code changed.

No findings.
